proposals.title: Main skips crypto
proposals.why: In crypto the market scores a Brier of 0.034 against Jev+research's 0.117 (9 resolved), so any edge we think we see there is most likely our own error. This is an experiment on a small sample.
proposals.judge_by: On the yardstick, main's P&L on bets opened after this change is at least original's. Meanwhile, original's crypto bets over the same period lose money in total.
proposals.status_reason: main rules v2: skips none → crypto

proposals.title: Bold meets the info gate halfway
proposals.why: Bold's extra bets, where Jev's info rating is 0.2–0.5, are losing $31.79 per $100 (7 bets), and main's info-stopped markets lose $70 per $100 (16). A 0.35 threshold tests where the cutoff really belongs, without collapsing bold into a copy of main.
proposals.judge_by: Bold's P&L per $100 staked since the change beats its old -$31.79 per $100, and is closer to or above main's over the same period.

proposals.title: Claude direct, pickier and without crypto
proposals.why: Claude is our best forecaster (Brier 0.132 on 24) yet lost all 3 of its settled bets. The places where it disagrees with the market by only 8% are probably where the market is right. This challenger demands a 12% edge, skips crypto, and bets half as much per bet.
proposals.judge_by: Positive P&L, and more P&L per $100 staked than claude_direct over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: retired by the daily review 2026-10-04: ch3 has placed 5 bets in 5 days and lost all 3 settled (-$60 per $100). At that pace it would take months to reach 30 results. It differs from claude_direct only by a higher edge bar and a smaller sta

proposals.title: Break results down by price paid
proposals.why: Many losses, including all 3 of claude_direct's and every info-gate-stopped group, show -$100 per $100, meaning the whole stake was lost. That pattern suggests we may be buying cheap longshots. A breakdown of wins and P&L by ask price (for example <0.2, 0.2–0.5, 0.5–0.8, >0.8), for placed and stopped bets, would let us set min_ask and max_ask from evidence instead of guessing.
proposals.judge_by: The review data includes a by-price breakdown, and within 2 reviews it leads to either a min_ask/max_ask tune or a clear finding that price doesn't matter.

proposals.title: Jev alone, bold: pickier, no crypto or economy
proposals.why: Jev alone scores worse than the market in every category, with a Brier of 0.221 against 0.052 in crypto (21 resolved) and 0.294 against 0.168 in economy (12 resolved). This strategy has lost $17 per $100 staked (22 bets, 6 settled). The experiment is to demand a bigger edge and skip Jev's worst categories, while leaving the info gate at 0.2 so it stays distinct from Jev alone.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, P&L per $100 staked beats its all-time -$17.4 per $100 and is at least as good as jev_alone over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: jev_alone_bold rules v2: edge bar 8% → 12%; skips none → crypto, economy

proposals.title: Jev + research, picky
proposals.why: Bets main actually placed have lost $15 per $100 (7 settled), and Jev + research trails the market badly in crypto and economy. This tests whether requiring a 15% edge, and dropping both categories, turns research-driven bets profitable. It can run now, while main is locked until tomorrow.
proposals.judge_by: P&L per $100 staked is at or above zero, and above original's on the markets both bet over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: retired by the daily review 2026-10-03: ch6 has settled 2 bets, lost both, and is down $4.0k. Its idea is to bet only where Jev disagrees with the market by 15+ points, but the market out-forecasts Jev + research (0.150 vs 0.201 Brier over

proposals.title: Paired Brier scores and a calibration sanity check
proposals.why: Each source is scored on a different set of markets (Claude on 33, the market on 120), so 'Claude beats the market' can't be trusted. The calibration map has a=1.489, and its forecasts score worse than raw Jev (0.236 against 0.199), even though reviews blame Jev being overconfident. A=1.489 may be stretching forecasts further from 50/50 instead of pulling them back.
proposals.judge_by: Joey approves, and the next review shows Brier scores for each source against the market on the same resolved markets, plus the calibrated source's score on markets the map wasn't fitted to.
proposals.status_reason: approved by Joey 2026-10-02; needs a code session

proposals.title: Score forecasters on 30c+ markets only
proposals.why: Since 2026-10-01 every strategy bets only at 30c or more, but the Brier table (market 0.114 vs our best 0.121) mixes in the long shots we no longer touch. We need to know whether any forecaster beats the price where we actually bet, matched market by market.
proposals.judge_by: The review data gains each source's Brier score next to the market's on the same resolved markets priced 30c or more. Success means Joey can see whether any source scores below the market there, which decides which challenger to start next.

proposals.title: Shrink forecasts toward the market before computing edge
proposals.why: The market's Brier (0.123, 201 markets) beats every forecaster, and most of our losses came from bets where we disagreed with it most, such as long shots that went 1 for 21. A strategy option that blends the forecast with the market price (for example 50/50) before the edge check would bet only where a disagreement survives that discount. The forecasters themselves would still never see the price.
proposals.judge_by: Replay the blended rule on resolved markets that were judged after the code ships, and compare it with the unblended rule on the same markets. It succeeds if settled P&L per $100 is higher and it has fewer losing bets.

proposals.title: Gate ledger and price breakdown for 30c+ markets only
proposals.why: The gate ledger mixes in long shots, which lost 1 in 42 before the floor. That makes every 'stopped by the info gate' number look worse than it would under today's rules: calibrated's info-stopped markets show −$7.1 per $100 (66) and main's −$24.6 (78). We can't sensibly tune the info gates until the ledger shows only markets the 30c floor would let through.
proposals.judge_by: The next reviews show a 30c+ gate ledger and a by_price_paid split for each strategy's since_change bets. It is worth having if it changes or confirms an info-gate decision once there is enough data.

proposals.title: Pooled tally of bets placed under the floor
proposals.why: Each strategy has 0–1 settled bets since 2026-10-01, so the floor's '30 settled bets' test will take weeks per strategy. Pooling every strategy's 30c+ bets placed since the floor, measured against original's long shots over the same period, would answer whether the floor pays much sooner.
proposals.judge_by: The review reports pooled P&L per $100 on 30c+ bets since 2026-10-01 alongside original's under-30c bets. The floor is confirmed if the pooled result beats original's long shots.

proposals.title: Retire ch6 (picky Jev + research)
proposals.why: ch6 has settled 2 bets, lost both, and is down $4.0k. Its idea is to bet only where Jev disagrees with the market by 15+ points, but the market out-forecasts Jev + research (0.150 vs 0.201 Brier over 191 shared markets). Two results are noise, so this is a judgment call: the slot is better spent on a different hypothesis.
proposals.judge_by: No later check: its 3 open bets settle and are recorded, and the slot goes to the challenger below.
proposals.status_reason: ch6 retired; its open bets still settle and its record stays on the page

proposals.title: Calibrated, favourites only
proposals.why: Across strategies, bets on favourites (60c and up) have gone 12 wins to 6 losses. The calibrated forecaster went 5 for 5 there (+$3.6k), and main 2 for 2 (+$1.4k). This tests whether calibrated Jev makes money when it only backs prices of 55c and above. It is an experiment on tiny numbers.
proposals.judge_by: P&L per $100 staked is positive, and better than the calibrated strategy's over the same period.

proposals.title: Bold skips crypto, like main
proposals.why: In crypto, Jev + research scores 0.151 against the market's 0.087 over 56 resolved markets. Bold is down $20.3k, the worst of any strategy, on 33 settled. Skipping crypto leaves bold differing from main only in its info gate (0.35 vs 0.5), which makes it a clean test of that gate.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, bold's P&L per $100 staked beats its current all-time -$22 per $100, and is within $10 per $100 of main's over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: bold rules v4: skips none → crypto

proposals.title: Retire ch3 (Claude direct, strict)
proposals.why: ch3 has placed 5 bets in 5 days and lost all 3 settled (-$60 per $100). At that pace it would take months to reach 30 results. It differs from claude_direct only by a higher edge bar and a smaller stake, so the slot is better spent on a sharper question.
proposals.judge_by: Success means the replacement challenger places more bets per day than ch3's 1 per day, so its results arrive faster.
proposals.status_reason: ch3 retired; its open bets still settle and its record stays on the page

proposals.title: Claude direct, sports only
proposals.why: In sports, Claude direct scores 0.151 Brier on 67 markets against the market's 0.176 across all 232 sports markets. This is the only category where any of our sources looks better than the price. The two scores cover different sets of markets, so the comparison is suggestive only. Two-thirds of Claude's forecasts are sports, so this isolates its best area without starving the strategy of bets.
proposals.judge_by: Success means P&L per $100 staked is at least 0 and beats claude_direct's 30c+ bets over the same period. If it is below -$20 per $100 after 30 settled bets, retire it.

proposals.title: Claimed edge vs realised return
proposals.why: Every source is worse than the market, yet each bet claims at least 8c of edge. Bucketing settled 30c+ bets by claimed edge (8-12c, 12-20c, 20c+) and showing win rate and P&L per $100 would show whether big claimed edges are real edges or big errors. That would tell us whether to raise or lower min_edge.
proposals.judge_by: Success means Joey approves the table and it reports per-bucket P&L for each strategy. We then use it to set min_edge.

proposals.title: Claude direct demands a bigger edge
proposals.why: Claude direct's forecasts trail the market (paired Brier 0.182 vs 0.153 on 357 markets), so its 8c 'edges' are probably mostly error. Its bets lose $68 per $100 (9 settled). This is an experiment; ch3 tried a pickier Claude direct and was retired, but it did that without the 30c floor.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, P&L per $100 staked beats claude_direct's all-time -$51 per $100 and is no worse than main's over the same period.

proposals.title: Jev alone, bold stops buying favourites
proposals.why: Jev alone, bold has lost all 3 of its bets at 60c and up (-$6.0k), while its 30-60c bets are +$914 on 6. Jev alone is the weakest forecaster (Brier 0.235), and paying 60c+ leaves little room for its error. This rests on only 3 bets, so it is an experiment.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, P&L per $100 staked beats its since-floor -$4.9 per $100 and its all-time -$43 per $100.
proposals.status_reason: jev_alone_bold rules v4: highest price none → 60¢

proposals.title: Calibrated vs main on the same markets
proposals.why: Calibrated's profit (+$3.4k on 9 settled since the floor) contrasts with its Brier of 0.210, slightly worse than raw Jev + research at 0.2065. So its edge may come from which bets it picks and how it sizes them, or it may be luck. A paired comparison would show whether the calibration itself earns money before anyone considers moving main onto it.
proposals.judge_by: Report calibrated's and main's P&L per $100 on markets both bet, and on markets only one bet, since 2026-10-01. If calibrated is ahead by more than $10 per $100 on the shared markets after 30 resolved, consider giving main the calibrated forecasts.

proposals.title: Sports-only Claude gets more bets
proposals.why: Sports is the only category where any forecaster beats the market (Claude 0.158 vs market 0.176, on 131 markets), yet ch16 has placed 1 bet in about 2.5 days. The 4 markets stopped only by Jev's info gate would have paid +$77 per $100. Jev's own information rating may say little about Claude's forecast. This is an experiment on tiny numbers.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, ch16's P&L per $100 staked is positive and ahead of claude_direct's over the same period.

proposals.title: Price breakdown since each strategy's last rule change
proposals.why: by_price_paid is all-time, so pre-floor long shots dominate it: about $100k of losses on 73 bets. That hides whether 30-60c and 60c+ bets pay under the current rules. Bold's -$5.5k and calibrated's +$5.0k in favourites can't be dated to a rule version.
proposals.judge_by: The review shows since-change wins and P&L per price bucket for every strategy, and the next favourites or max_ask decision cites it.

proposals.title: Main demands a bigger edge
proposals.why: Jev + research trails the market by about 0.06 Brier on 559 paired markets, so many of its 8c 'edges' are probably forecast error. Main loses about $26 per $100 since the floor (11 settled) and trails original per dollar on the yardstick (-$32 vs -$22 per $100). Requiring 12c, as claude_direct now does, tests whether fewer, stronger-conviction bets lose less. This is an experiment on small numbers.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, main's P&L per $100 staked on the yardstick (shared markets) is better than original's over the same period, and better than main's since-floor -$26 per $100. If main places fewer than 10 bets in a week, revert to 0.08.

proposals.title: Favourites-only challenger loosens its info gate
proposals.why: ch13 has placed only 5 bets in about 4.5 days. The 30 markets it skipped only because of Jev's info gate would have returned +$4.15 per $100 (19 wins), the only gate-blocked group in the ledger with a meaningful count that shows a profit. Lowering the gate from 0.5 to 0.35, bold's setting, should give it more bets at 55c and up. This is an experiment on noisy numbers.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, ch13 places at least 2 bets a day, and its P&L per $100 staked is positive and no worse than calibrated's over the same period.

proposals.title: Report settled stake separately from open stake
proposals.why: Most of our judge_by tests use 'P&L per $100 staked since the change', but the reported stake includes open bets. Bold has 14 of 41 bets open and ch16 has 8 of 10, so the per-$100 figures look better than they are. Splitting settled stake from open stake would let us judge p14, p18, p19, p21, p23 and p24 honestly.
proposals.judge_by: all_time, since_change and yardstick each report a settled_staked field, and the next review can compute P&L per $100 on settled bets only for every strategy.

proposals.title: Claude direct sticks to sports and culture
proposals.why: Claude trails the market badly outside sports: politics 0.255 vs 0.117 (13 markets), weather 0.208 vs 0.072 (19), other 0.138 vs 0.099 (19), crypto 0.134 vs 0.110 (37). It beats the market in sports (0.161 vs 0.177, 146 markets) and probably in culture (0.040 vs 0.089, but only 5 markets). Since its edge rose to 12c it has settled only 2 bets, so this is an experiment. It also sets up a comparison with ch16: a strict sports Claude (12c edge, info gate 0.5) against a loose one (8c edge, info gate 0.2).
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, Claude direct's P&L per $100 staked is positive and beats its all-time -$55 per $100. We also compare it with ch16's over the same period to see whether the strict or the loose sports setup earns more per $100.
proposals.status_reason: claude_direct rules v4: skips none → crypto, economy, other, politics, tech, weather, world

proposals.title: Calibrated skips crypto, politics and economy
proposals.why: Jev + research trails the market most in crypto (0.168 vs 0.104 on 152 markets), politics (0.260 vs 0.117 on 45) and economy (0.232 vs 0.103 on 42). Main and bold already skip crypto, but calibrated, the best-performing Jev strategy (-$2.7k on 17 settled since the price floor), does not.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, calibrated's settled P&L per $100 staked beats its since-floor figure of about -$6 per $100. That figure includes open stake, so it is approximate. It should also be no worse than main's over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: calibrated rules v3: skips none → crypto, economy, politics

proposals.title: Measure skill per category as well as per source
proposals.why: Claude's pooled edge over the market is negative (-0.020 on 564 markets), which keeps ch16 on probe bets forever, even though Claude beats the market in sports (0.167 vs 0.178 on 152). Measuring lambda for each source and category pair, with the same 300-market threshold, would let a real pocket of skill size up without loosening the rule anywhere else.
proposals.judge_by: If Joey approves, the review shows lambda for each source and category pair. We then check whether Claude in sports reaches a positive lambda on 300 or more markets, and whether ch16's P&L per $100 stays positive once it sizes by Kelly.

proposals.title: Bold bets on sports only
proposals.why: Jev + research trails the market least in sports (0.205 vs 0.178 on 539 markets) and far more elsewhere: politics 0.260 vs 0.117, economy 0.232 vs 0.103, other 0.232 vs 0.103, weather 0.219 vs 0.085. Bold's info-gate test has told us little: markets stopped only by that gate lose about the same as bets placed (-$31 vs -$31 per $100 on 167 and 62), so bold's slot is better spent testing whether Jev + research can earn in its best category. This is an experiment.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, bold's settled P&L per $100 staked beats its v4 figure of about -$9 per $100 and beats main's over the same period. If bold places fewer than 1 bet a day, restore its previous categories.
proposals.status_reason: bold rules v5: skips crypto → crypto, culture, economy, other, politics, tech, weather, world

proposals.title: Find out why Sharp line has never bet
proposals.why: The Sharp (Pinnacle) strategy shows 0 bets, 0 open and n=0 in the skill table, while every other source has hundreds of judged markets. Either its price feed never matches our markets or its 3c edge and 20-85c price band filter out everything. Without bets we can't learn whether a sharp bookmaker line beats the prediction-market price.
proposals.judge_by: A short diagnostic report showing, per cycle, how many markets got a Sharp probability and which gate stopped each one. Then either Sharp places probe bets or we know why it can't.

proposals.title: Sanity-check the skill estimate before it drives sizing
proposals.why: Every source shows a standard error of exactly 0.0. Sharp line shows raw skill 23.593 on just 7 markets, while the others sit around -0.03, so the scale looks wrong. If lambda turns positive with a bad error estimate or a bad scale, Kelly sizing could bet far too much.
proposals.judge_by: The next report shows non-zero standard errors for every source with n > 0, and Sharp's raw skill on the same scale as the others (well under 1). Joey confirms how lambda handles small samples.

proposals.title: Yardstick split since main's last rule change
proposals.why: Main's 12c-edge test (p23) is to be judged on yardstick P&L for bets opened after 2026-10-07. The report only gives the yardstick since 2026-09-29: main -$17.4k on 24 settled, original -$15.9k on 37. Those figures mix old rules with new.
proposals.judge_by: The report shows main vs original on shared markets opened since main's current rules took effect, with settled counts. That lets us judge p23 on 2026-10-14, when main can change again.

proposals.title: Sharp line asks for a 2c edge instead of 3c
proposals.why: Sharp has placed 1 bet ever under a 3c-after-fees edge requirement, so we are learning nothing about whether Pinnacle's line beats these prices. A de-vigged sharp line is a strong forecaster, and a 2c edge is a reasonable experiment while sizing is probe-only anyway. If the real cause is a matching or data bug (p30), this change will do nothing, and that itself tells us something.
proposals.judge_by: Within 3 days sharp places at least 1 bet a day. If it doesn't, the bottleneck is coverage, not the edge requirement, and this should be reverted. After enough settle, its settled P&L per $100 staked is zero or better.

proposals.title: Point Claude direct's forecasts at sports first
proposals.why: Claude direct is the only source that beats the market in any category (sports, 0.169 vs 0.177), but it has forecast only 174 of 717 resolved sports markets. Meanwhile claude_direct placed 1 bet since its last change and ch16 places about 1 a day. Within the existing budget, giving sports markets priority for Claude direct forecasts should give both strategies more bets where the edge actually exists.
proposals.judge_by: Over the week after it ships, the share of resolved sports markets with a Claude direct forecast rises well above today's 24%, ch16 and claude_direct place more bets per day, and Claude's sports Brier stays below the market's.

proposals.title: Restore the missing strategies to the daily review
proposals.why: This review lists only sharp, mention_no and mention_follow, and the yardstick is empty. Yet the log shows original placing a bet this period, and main, bold, calibrated, claude_direct and jev_alone_bold all have live experiments (p23, p26, p27, p29) waiting to be judged. Tuning blind would be guessing.
proposals.judge_by: The next review lists every running strategy with all_time, since_change and by_price_paid, and has a non-empty yardstick comparing main with original.

proposals.title: Check that sharp's 2c edge change was actually applied
proposals.why: The rule-change log records sharp at version 2 with min_edge 0.02 since 2026-10-11, but sharp's current rules show version 1, min_edge 0.03, rules_changed null and locked. If the change never applied, p33's '1 bet a day within 3 days' test is invalid. Sharp's skill of -1.63 on 28 markets also looks like a scoring or matching bug (see p30).
proposals.judge_by: Joey confirms which min_edge sharp is actually using and when it took effect, and the sharp skill figure is either explained or fixed. If 2c is now in force, p33's 3-day clock restarts from that date.

proposals.title: Make by_price_paid count open bets consistently
proposals.why: Sharp's price buckets count its 1 bet, but mention_no's 32 open bets appear in no bucket at all, even though its 30-70c price band means they must fall in 30-60c or 60c+. When these settle, the long-shot/favourite comparison behind the 30c floor will be wrong for mention strategies.
proposals.judge_by: In the next review, mention_no's bucket bet counts add up to its all-time 32 or more, and settled P&L by bucket matches its total P&L once bets resolve.

proposals.title: Alert when a cycle judges nothing
proposals.why: 48 cycles in 12 hours judged 0 markets with 0 research while 45 markets resolved, so the forecasting pipeline seems stalled or starved of new markets. A stall like this silently freezes every Jev and Claude strategy.
proposals.judge_by: Joey finds the cause of the 0-judged half-day. Then any run of 6 or more consecutive cycles with 0 judged markets raises a flag in the next review. In the next full review, judged is above 0 and Jev and Claude strategies place bets again.

proposals.title: Explain sharp's skill estimate of -1.56
proposals.why: A raw skill of -1.5581 on 29 markets is far outside the range of the other sources (-0.01 to -0.02). It points to a matching or units bug in how Pinnacle's line is paired with Kalshi prices, probably the same cause as sharp's near-zero bet count (p30). This is narrower than p31's general sanity check and should be fixed before sharp's forward test is read.
proposals.judge_by: After the fix, sharp's raw skill on the same markets lies between -0.1 and +0.1. A spot check of 5 of its 29 markets shows the sharp probability and the market price refer to the same outcome.

proposals.title: Hold Claude direct's Kelly sizing until its skill estimate is checked
proposals.why: Claude direct's lambda turned positive (0.0091, n=783) while it trails the market by 0.038 Brier on 783 paired markets, and its raw skill of 0.042 sits inside one standard error (0.078). Real Kelly sizing should not start on a number that contradicts the Brier comparison. This is a concrete instance of p31.
proposals.judge_by: Joey either explains why a positive lambda is consistent with Claude's paired Brier being worse than the market's, or keeps Claude direct on probe bets until lambda's lower bound (raw minus 1 standard error) is above 0. Checked at the next review after the fix.

proposals.title: Find out why 48 cycles judged nothing
proposals.why: In the past 12 hours there were 48 cycles, 0 markets judged, 0 researched, and no Jev or Claude bets, while 41 markets resolved. p38 only adds an alert; this asks for the cause. It may be the same fault that dropped main and the other strategies from this review (p35).
proposals.judge_by: The next 12-hour review shows judged > 0, bets from Jev or Claude strategies, and main, original and the yardstick present again.

proposals.title: Skill estimate reports a standard error of 0 for six of seven sources
proposals.why: Every source except Claude direct shows se 0.0 and lambda 0, even mention_prior with raw +0.594 on 94 markets and jev_research on 1,183. A zero standard error on 1,000+ markets looks like a computation fallback, not a real estimate. It may be silently pinning these sources to probe bets, or would mis-size them once their raw skill turns positive. This is a narrower, concrete instance of what p31 and p39 ask about.
proposals.judge_by: After the fix, every source with 30+ priced, finished markets reports a nonzero se. mention_prior's lambda is then either positive or explained by a stated rule (for example, a minimum of 300 markets).

proposals.title: Hold the daily review until a health check passes
proposals.why: Today's input has 0 judged markets in 48 cycles and 3 of roughly 10 strategies, with no yardstick. Tuning on this would be guesswork, and the earlier flags for these problems (p35, p38, p41) are still unapproved. A pre-review check would stop us proposing changes against a broken feed: it would require markets judged in the last day, every live strategy present, and a non-empty yardstick.
proposals.judge_by: The next review either includes every live strategy, the yardstick and markets judged in the period, or it is replaced by a clear 'pipeline unhealthy' notice naming which check failed.

proposals.title: Check applied rule changes against the live rules
proposals.why: p33 is logged as applied and set sharp's min_edge to 0.02 (version 2). The live rules still read 0.03, version 1, with rules_changed null. If one applied change was silently lost, others may have been too, and every 'judge_by' since then would be measuring the wrong rules. A daily check of each applied proposal's version and values against the live config would catch this; it widens p36 from sharp to every strategy.
proposals.judge_by: The check runs once and lists any mismatches between recent_rule_changes and each strategy's live rules and rules_version. Sharp's mismatch is either fixed (shows version 2, min_edge 0.02) or explained.

proposals.title: Reconcile sharp's ledger with its record and live rules
proposals.why: Sharp's gate ledger shows 1 bet placed and lost (-$100 per $100), but its all-time record shows 0 bets. Its live rules show min_edge 0.03 at version 1, even though the 10-11 change to 0.02 (version 2) is logged as applied. Either bets or rule changes are being lost between the stores, so any verdict on sharp, and possibly on other strategies, is unreliable until this is fixed. This is a concrete case for p36 and p44, and fixing it first may also explain p30.
proposals.judge_by: After the fix, sharp's all_time bet count equals its gate_ledger 'bet' count, and its rules show min_edge 0.02 at rules_version 2 (or the log shows why the change was undone). The next review then shows the same counts in both places.

proposals.title: Triage: restore judging and the missing strategies before any more tuning
proposals.why: With 0 judged in 48 cycles and every tunable strategy missing from the review, the only rules I can see belong to locked strategies, and tuning blind would only add noise. I suggest Joey take the open proposals in this order: p41 (why nothing is judged), p35 (missing strategies), p44 (applied changes vs live rules), then p40 and p31, because Claude's positive lambda could start Kelly-sized bets on an edge that isn't statistically real.
proposals.judge_by: The next review shows judged above 0 in recent cycles, lists main, original, bold, calibrated and claude_direct with since_change results, and shows a non-empty yardstick. Tuning resumes only after that.

proposals.title: One acceptance check for p46, and fold the duplicate diagnostics into it
proposals.why: p35, p36, p38, p41, p43, p44 and p45 all describe the same failure: 0 markets judged in 48 cycles, missing strategies, and sharp's rules not matching the change log. Each review has added another near-duplicate instead of a fix. Every strategy we are allowed to tune is invisible, and the three we can see are locked, so tuning is blocked until this is fixed.

proposals.title: Mention NO: wins and losses don't match its P&L
proposals.why: In the 30-60c band, mention_no shows 5 wins and 11 losses on $631 staked, yet a profit of $111. With every price at or above the 30c floor, that is impossible unless the wins and losses are counted from the YES side or the P&L includes something else. Mention_follow's numbers do add up, so the fault looks specific to NO-side bets.
proposals.judge_by: Joey confirms which figure is wrong. After the fix, recomputing each band from its bets gives P&L consistent with the win/loss counts and the prices paid, to within fees, for every strategy shown.

proposals.title: Check mention_prior's skill before Kelly sizing starts
proposals.why: mention_prior just passed 300 markets with lambda 0.08, so mention_no moves from probe bets to Kelly sizing. But its standard error (0.34) is larger than its raw estimate (0.24), and mention_follow shows a raw 2.73 on only 11 markets, which suggests the estimator is unstable for these sources (see p31 and p42). This is the mention-source counterpart of p40.
proposals.judge_by: Before mention_no's next Kelly-sized bet, a check either confirms the estimate (it stays positive when recomputed on settled bets only) or holds sizing at probe until the standard error is below the estimate.
